versions.title_at_revision: Electrical components and cables vibratory response
versions.text: Criterion: Verify all engine electrical components and associated cabling do not react to engine or air vehicle induced vibratory and acoustic excitations. Standard: All components and cabling are designed such that their natural frequencies are outside the engine and air vehicle operating range or have adequate damping provisions to prevent resonances, damage or failure. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, inspection and review of documentation. Analysis of vibration surveys and vibration (shaker table) testing on components and cabling verifies capability to operate in the expected vibratory environment and that natural frequencies are outside the engine operating range. Full-up engine testing, with vibration measuring instrumentation, provides assurance that electrical components and cabling can safely operate within the engine operating envelope. Inspection of all components and cabling after engine testing verifies no wear, chafing, stretching and/or damage exists. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.4.1.5.1.1 - A.3.4.1.5.1.2, A.4.4.1.5.1.1 - A.4.4.1.5.1.2; A.4.11.2.1.5.2, 14 CFR 33.63, 33.83

Standard: Electrical cables are designed to ensure their natural frequencies are outside the engine and air vehicle operating range. Cables are routed and affixed to provide damping, to prevent damaging resonances. Damaging vibration and resonances do not occur in the operating speed range from 20% below idle speed to 20% above maximum operating speed. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation (e.g., hardware drawings, system configuration descriptions, materials and manufacturing records, design data records, inspection reports, photographs, ICD, or other substantiating records and reports) to verify the design of the electrical cables. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis verifies electrical cables natural frequencies are outside the engine and air vehicle operating range.
  (2) Analysis verifies electrical cables withstand excitations resulting from a full blade out condition. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Vibration surveys (ping testing) and vibration (shaker table) testing verifies the natural frequencies of the engine cables are outside the engine and air vehicle operating range.
    (2) Lab test: Engine ground-based sea level cell testing, with vibration measuring instrumentation verifies the natural frequencies of the engine cables are outside the engine and air vehicle operating range.
